title: how synthetic edges stay alive across incremental patches
summary: Synthetic edges are never stored in the index — they are re-derived from scratch on every build AND every incremental patch, which is the only reason they survive an edit at all, because patchIndex replaces a changed file's symbolEdges wholesale and strips both directions of its flat edges on delete. The re-derivation inside patch is gated on the CHANGED FILE'S LANGUAGE (changedLangs.has('ruby') etc.), so any future synthetic-edge family whose input is not a source file of that language — e.g. one derived from the notebook — would never be refreshed by an ordinary code edit and needs its own trigger. A synthetic edge whose endpoint file no longer exists is not merely ignored: lintIndexInvariants check 3 reports it and the keeper queues a full rebuild, and since a rebuild re-runs the same derivation, a derivation that keeps emitting a dead endpoint rebuilds forever. Derivations must therefore filter endpoints against index.files themselves.

steps.role: replaces a changed file's symbol edges wholesale, then re-runs each synthetic-edge family gated on the changed languages
flags any symbol edge whose asserted file side is absent from index.files; a violation makes the keeper rebuild

invariants: Synthetic edges are a derivation, never persisted data — anything written into the index by hand is wiped on the next patch of that file.
Every synthetic-edge derivation must drop endpoints not present in index.files, or invariant check 3 turns into a rebuild loop.
assertedFile deliberately exempts bare extends/implements targets from the existence check; only refs carrying a '#' (and the exports edge's from-side) assert a file.
